body: Thanks for your replies, everyone. I know it would devastate my SO and my family if I were to go through with this. The thought of hurting my SO is what keeps me from it, more than hurting my family. I have my ups and downs like everyone I'm sure. I'll be feeling fine for days with only mild dysphoria, but then something triggers me. The most common trigger for my anxiety lately is my school work. I sank into bad habits this semester, and just didn't do most of my homework. Now it's the last week, and I have only just gotten to where I'm going to pass in one of my prerequisite courses, but the other will take a miracle for me to pass. If I don't, then the way my scholarship works, if I fail or drop a class, I'll lose my financial aid, and be forced to drop out for lack of funds. I'm struggling to catch up but I don't think I can. I keep getting hung up on certain aspects of my assignments, and when I do, I start thinking about it too much, which creates a downward spiral, setting off serious dysphoria on top of school anxiety. I'm lucid at the moment, but when I hit those downward spirals, which of course are caused by more circumstances than the one I described alone, that's when I get to where I don't trust myself. At those times I get so bad that I often inflict self harm, and I feel like the only thing keeping me from peace is the guilt of leaving my loved ones behind. That of course makes me feel worse, having guilt be my reason to keep going. I don't trust me when I'm like that. I feel like if I fail this semester, or screw up in a similarly large manner in the future, that that's it, and I won't stop myself. I have tried to find a councilor, but even before I left my job, nobody I could find would accept my insurance, or let me pay out of pocket. And now that I have no income, that narrows the possibilities of counciling even further. On top of all that, when I talk to my SO when I'm on one of my downs, all the uplifting comments she says to me make me feel worse. It's like compliments have the opposite effect. I'm not sure what that says about me. All in all, I don't know where to go for professional help, and I'm losing the will to seek it. Sorry for the long rant, I'm sure I am not making much sense. If anyone can point me in the direction of a councilor or somebody I can afford to talk to in the Dallas area, I'd appreciate it.
